article: Frederick Fawcett, The Saoras of Madras, Journal of the Anthropological Society of Bombay 1 no. 4 (1888), 206–272
article_extent_evidence: Existing lead README; article opening and final page not independently verified in this pass.
decision: Yes: all 41 aligned source responses are target-language attestations. Their possessive/recursive structure is not a valid exclusion under the whole-source policy. Recover the complete expressions with literal source glosses; no inferred free kinship lemmas.
previous_exclusion: README excluded the entire table solely because responses contain Mian and nested relations. Superseded in scope only; no canonical ingestion performed.
source_provenance: P227 says an unnamed Uriya speaker who knew Saora wrote the tables; Fawcett reviewed them with an unnamed Saora speaker for pronunciation. He calls the transcription Missionary alphabet and explicitly disclaims exact pronunciation.
specific_scope_requirements: Inspect every article page 206–272 for quoted target words, names, expressions, songs, grammar, tables and explicit non-target controls.
Read p225 personal-name anecdotes as source claims rather than automatically exclude all names.
Resolve ditto marks in both columns against explicit antecedents; maintain raw cells.
Retain m. s./f. s. distinctions with source expansion only when supplied.
Preserve stress footnotes: p226 * last syllable and dagger second syllable; p227 * second syllable of last word and dagger second and last syllables of last word.
Do not normalize p227 Main to p226 Mian or commas to IPA syllable boundaries without source evidence.
availability: Only two distinct local original page images located; duplicate (1) copies also exist outside Jambu and were not modified. No full article PDF located in Jambu scratch.
